title: What surprised you
hook: the thing you didn't expect to learn

segments.voice: Yesterday, the world, and your line: everywhere. Languages and colors as signs, and one body that feels its far limbs. What news reached you from far away? Day one thousand four hundred twenty.

A boat pulls away from the shore with two travelers aboard. Once they are on board, one of them sets to work knocking a hole in its side. The other is Musa, a prophet, and he cannot believe what he is seeing. In Surat al-Kahf he had set out on this journey to learn, and promised his teacher, a servant of Allah given knowledge from Allah's own presence, that he would be patient. He lasts until the boat. Today, after a year of learning, the thing you didn't expect.
screen: `A HOLE IN THE BOAT.` → `A PROPHET WHO PROMISED PATIENCE.` → `WHAT YOU DIDN'T EXPECT.`

segments.voice: First, the surprises. In the Qur'an's telling, the boat is only the beginning. Musa protests. Then a second act, far harder, and Musa cries out against it. Then, in a town that refused them food, the man rebuilds a falling wall for nothing. Musa says he could at least have taken pay. Each time the man reminds him, in paraphrase: did I not say you could not be patient with me? Second, the explanations. The boat belonged to poor people, and a king was seizing every boat by force, and a damaged one would be passed by. Under the wall lay a treasure belonging to two orphan boys whose father had been righteous, kept safe until they were grown. What looked wrong was something Musa did not yet know. Hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari name the man al-Khidr; the Qur'an simply calls him one of Allah's servants. Third, what the story does with surprise. Musa was a prophet, and he still had more to learn, and the learning arrived as surprise. The Qur'an elsewhere gives the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, a line to say: "My Lord! Increase me in knowledge." Surprise can be what that request looks like when it is answered. Fourth, your own year. Maybe it was that hadith scholars tested the words as well as the chain. Or that, in Sahih al-Bukhari, Allah divided mercy into a hundred parts and sent down only one. Or that people of different schools stand in one row and no one corrects anyone. Or something else entirely, that did not go the way you expected.
screen: `A BOAT, A SECOND ACT, A WALL.` · `WHAT LOOKED WRONG WAS NOT YET KNOWN.` · `INCREASE ME IN KNOWLEDGE.` · `WHAT DID THIS YEAR SURPRISE?`

segments.voice: The practice: write it down. First, the sit. Settle, and breathe. Let the year go by slowly, like pages turning: the pillars, the reports, the schools, the creed, the heart, the manners, the life cycle, the world. Somewhere in there, one thing may catch, a moment of wait, really? Don't choose the most impressive one. Choose the one that actually caught. Hold it for the rest of the sit. When the bell rings, write it down in one sentence, somewhere you will find it again. The bell holds the time.
What surprised you. The moment a year of learning went somewhere you did not expect, which in Musa's story is where the learning really began. Today's word.

Your line: surprised. Today, tell one person the thing that surprised you this year, in a sentence, and see whether it surprises them too. Tomorrow, what changed in practice. Day one thousand four hundred twenty.

howItsDone: Muslims read the story of Musa and al-Khidr in Surat al-Kahf, which some recite on Fridays, and teachers use it to speak about humility in learning and the limits of what a person can see.

fork.setup: you're Musa. your teacher has just knocked a hole in the boat that carried you. you promised to be patient. what do you do?
fork.reveal: Musa protests, and is reminded: did I not say you could not be patient with me? the explanation comes only at the end.

original.note: Arabic: wonder, a marvel, the thing that makes you stop and stare.

trapdoor: what you thought: a surprise is a thing you got wrong.
what it means: in Musa's story, surprise is where learning starts, the moment you meet what you did not yet know.
what a scholar hears: Surat al-Kahf 18:60–82, the servant given knowledge from Allah's presence, Bukhari's naming of al-Khidr, and 20:114.

notes: Confirm Pickthall's wording of 20:114 ('My Lord! Increase me in knowledge.').
The second act (the killing of the boy, 18:74, 18:80–81) is mentioned only as 'a second act, far harder'; a Keeper should decide whether to name it.
The year's surprises offered as examples recall days 1146, 1266 and 1213.
howItsDone 'which some recite on Fridays' has no cited text here; the Friday recitation of al-Kahf rests on hadith such as al-Hakim/Bayhaqi. Soften or cut if needed.
